senses: to give, put, bring forth, come forth
to generate, produce, propagate, bear, beget
to put forth in writing; publish, relate, report, record
to proclaim, announce, publish, make known
to reveal, disclose; betray perfidiously, surrender treacherously
to permit to go farther, protract, project; put off, defer; prolong; hand down; bequeath
la:verb:prodo.html:
prō-do, dĭdi, dĭtum, 3 (archaic produit for prodiderit, = porro dederit, porticum sartam tectamque habeto, prodito, Lex Censor. ap. Müll.;
pres. part. abl. sing. prodente, ), v. a.
To give, put, or bring forth (class.; syn. edo, profero, promo): prodit fumoso condita vina cado,: suspiria pectore,: hydraulam et choraulam,to show,: exemplum turpe,to give a bad example,: perniciosum exemplum,: prodendi exempli causā,of setting an example,.—
In partic.
To bring forth, bear, produce (poet.): parvā prodite patriā, Att. ap. : quae tam festa dies ut cesset prodere furem, Perfidiam, fraudes,.—
To put forth in writing, i. e. to publish, make known, relate, report, record: cum decretum proditur, lex veri rectique proditur,: Procilius non idem prodidit, quod Piso,: ea, quae scriptores Graeciae prodiderunt,: haec monumenta nobis litterae prodiderunt,: Thucydides ossa ejus clam ab amicis esse sepulta, memoriae prodidit, has handed down to memory, i. e. has recorded, : hujus bella gesta multi memoriae prodiderunt,: ut produnt,as they say.: prodere aliquid memoriā, to put forth from memory, i. e. to record, relate: quos natos in insulā ipsā, memoriā proditum dicunt,: ut quod proditum memoriā est,.—Esp., to publish, proclaim any one as appointed to an office, i. e. to appoint, elect, create a public officer of any kind (syn.: creo, designo): cum populo agendi jus esto ei, quem produnt patres consulum creandorum ergo,; flaminem,: interregem,: dictatorem,; to make known, disclose, discover, betray, : homine prodente conscios,: crimen vultu,: tamquam prodiderim quidquid scio,: arcanum,.—
To betray perfidiously, surrender treacherously: si Brutum prodideritis, et deserueritis,: is me deseruit ac prodidit,; ; cf. : prodebas caput et salutem meam,: classem praedonibus,: hosti rempublicam,: patriam,.—
To give up, surrender, abandon: rem summam, Enn. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 411 Vahl.): suam vitam, et Pecuniam omnem,.—
To extend, permit to go farther.
To put off, defer (anteclass.), Müll.—
To prolong, = produco, de mendico male meretur qui ei dat quod edit, nam illi prodit vitam ad miseriam, —
To hand down, transmit, bequeath (class.): qui sacra suis posteris prodiderunt,: jus imaginis ad memoriam posteritatemque prodendae,: regnum a Tantalo proditum,.—
To propagate (poet.): qui genus alto a sanguine Teucri Proderet,.

la:verb:produco.gloss: to lead or bring forth, forward or out
senses: to lead or bring forth, forward or out
to conduct to; bring before, present
to draw or stretch out, lengthen, extend
to bring to light, disclose, expose
to bring forth, bear, beget; bring up, rear, educate

la:verb:produco.html:
prō-dūco, xi, ctum, 3 (produxe, for produxisse, Ter Ad. 4, 2, 22), v. a.,
to lead or bring forth, to lead forward or out.
Lit. (class.): fidicinam intus,: aliquem foras ante aedes,: aliquem e latebris,: castris omnem exercitum,: copias pro castris,.—Esp.
To bring before the people, senate, or a court: aliquem in conspectum populi Romani,: quempiam in contionem,: cum tribunis

plebis Curionem et Octavium consules produxisset, ; : harum rerum omnium auctores testesque,: productus pro rostris,to give evidence,: producti in circo Flaminio in contionem,: in judicium,to bring before a court,: aliquem in Sestium,: aliquem ad necem,.—

Of an actor, to represent, perform: nihil ab hoc (Roscio) pravum et perversum produci posse arbitrabantur,. —
To expose for sale: ancillam produxit, vendidit,: servos,; .—
To draw or place one thing before another (poet.): producere malo aliquam moram,: scamnum lecto,: nubila menti,.—
To draw or stretch out, to lengthen out, extend (poet. and post-Aug.): pelles dentibus,: ferrum incude,: supercilium madidā fuligine tactum,: lineas ex argento nigras,.—
To conduct to a place: non tu eum rus hinc modo Produxe aiebas?.—
To conduct to the grave, sc. a corpse or a funeral procession (poet.): nec te, tua funera, mater Produxi,: longum funus ad tumulos,.—
To lead or bring along, to bring away: qui et procurrentem retrahat, et cunctantem producat,to drag forward,.—
To bring to light, disclose, expose: occulta ad patres produxit crimina servus,. —
In partic.
To bring forth, bring into the world, to bear or beget: ego is sum qui te produxi pater,: liberos,; Lucil. ap. : magnanimos nos natura produxit,: quam te Thersitae similem producat Achilles,.— Of other subjects, to produce, make (postAug.): cibis utendum est carnem producentibus,: cum folia producere incipiunt fici,.—
= adduco in indicium, to bring forth to trial, (Zumpt); .—
To make to grow, to advance, promote (poet.): subolem. .—
In pronunciation, to lengthen, prolong (class.): inclitus dicimus brevi primā litterā, insanus productā,: syllabam,; .—
Trop.
To bring forward (to distinction), to raise, promote, advance (class.): producere aliquem ad aliquam dignitatem. : aliquem omni genere honoris,: quem tu non pro illius dignitate produxeras,: a quibus producti sunt, exsistunt eorum ipsorum tyranni,advanced to power,: beneficia, quae non producunt, nec honestiorem faciunt,.—
To lead, induce one to do any thing: producti sumus, ut loqueremur,: productus ad aliquid faciendum,.—
To draw or drag out, to lengthen out, prolong, protract (class.): producere pauperi vitam ad miseriam,: cenam,: convivium ad multam noctem vario sermone,: sermonem in multam noctem,: sermonem longius,: Varro .. vitam Naevii producit longius,i. e. represents him as having lived longer,: somnum ultra primam lucem,: rem in hiemem,: animas,lives,.—
To put off, to amuse, delude one with fallacious promises: aliquem falsā spe producere,: aliquem conditionibus,.—
Of time, to pass, spend (poet.): cyathos sorbillans diem,.—
To bring up, educate: audientem dicto, mater, produxisti filiam,: principes liberos,: laevo monitu pueros avaros,.—
To make, devise, produce, bring into use: nova (vocabula) quae genitor produxerit usus,.—
To plant, cultivate: quicunque primum te produxit, arbor,.—Hence, prōductus, a, um, P. a., lengthened, long, prolonged, protracted, etc. (class.): productiore cornu sinistro,drawn out, extended, Halm: productissimum flagellum,: commoditates corporis tam productae temporibus, : dolores longinquitate producti,: exitus (orationis),. 53, 213: productiora alia, et quasi immoderatius excurrentia,too long,; so, producta syllaba (opp. short),: nomen,formed by prolongation,: neve minor, neu sit quinto productior actu Fabula,longer,.—
Subst.: prōducta, ōrum, n., preferable things (a transl. of the Gr. τἁ προηγμένα): in vitā non ea, quae primario loco sunt, sed ea, quae secundum locum obtinent, προηγμένα, id est producta nominantur; quae vel ita appellemus (id erit verbum e verbo), vel promota, et remota, vel, ut dudum diximus, praeposita, vel praecipua; et illa rejecta,; cf. .—Hence, adv.: prōductē, in a lengthened manner, long (class.): producte dicere litteram, opp. breviter,: producte dicere syllabam, opp. correpte,.—Comp.: syllaba productius pronunciata,.

la:noun:prodromus.html:
prodrŏmus, i, m., = πρόδρομος.
A certain north-northeast wind that blows eight days before the rising of the dog-star: prodromi nulli,; .—
A kind of early fig, .

la:noun:proditio.html:
prōdĭtĭo, ōnis, f.
prodo
.
A discovering, betraying; a discovery, betrayal, treason, treachery (class.): multorum in nos perfidiam, insidias, proditionem notabis,: amicitiarum proditiones,: arcanorum,: id nefas proditione discussum est,: timor est proditio cogitationis auxiliorum,. —
A putting off, deferring; the right of deferring (ante-class.), Cato ap. Fest. s. v. prodidisse, p. 242 Müll.

la:noun:prodigium.html:
prōdĭgĭum, ii (
gen. plur. prodigiūm, Pac. ap. ), n.
for prodicium, from prodico
.
Lit., a prophetic sign, token, omen, portent, prodigy, in a good and (more freq.) in a bad sense (syn.: portentum, ostentum, monstrum): mittere, Att. ap. : multa prodigia vim ejus numenque declarant,: (lunam deficientem) nullum esse prodigium,; : laetum,: P. Clodius fatale portentum prodigiumque rei publicae,: (Catilina) monstrum atque prodigium,: non mihi jam furtum, sed monstrum ac prodigium videbatur,i. e. a monstrous and unnatural crime,; cf. : piare prodigia,: accipere aliquid in prodigium,: prodigii loco habere,: Harpyia Prodigium canit,: nuntiare,: divinitus factum,: prodigiorum perita,: prodigio par est cum nobilitate senectus,: propter multa prodigia libros Sibyllinos adiisse,.—Of miracles: signa et prodigia, et saep. —
Transf., a monster, prodigy: non ego sum prodigium,: prodigium triplex,: heu prodigia ventris!.

la:verb:prodeo.gloss: to go forth: to advance, to proceed
senses: to go forth: to advance, to proceed
to come forth: to appear, to emerge, to become manifest
to come up, to turn out, to become fashionable
la:verb:prodeo.html:
prōdĕo, ĭi, ĭtum, īre (lengthened anteclass. form, prodinunt, for prodeunt, Enn. ap. Müll.;
post-class., prodient, for prodibunt,), v. n.
pro-eo
, to go or come forth (class.; cf.: proficiscor, progredior).
Lit.: prodinunt famuli, Enn. l. l.: prodi atque ostium aperi,: foras,to come out of doors,; ; : nemon' huc prodit?: in conspectum,: ex portu,: in aciem,: ad colloquium,: in publicum,: obviam alicui,to go to meet one,: in contionem,: in scenam,to come upon the stage, make one's appearance, praef.; ; .—Of soldiers in battle: in proelium,: in aciem,: in hostem,.—With simple abl.: utero matris prodire,: foribus,: tumulo,.—
Transf.
Of plants, to come forth, spring or grow up, appear: ea seges serius prodit,: prodeuntia semina,; : herba,.—
Of elevations, to stand out, project: et immodico prodibant tubere tali,; .—
Trop.
To come forth, show itself, appear (class.): novae quae prodeunt comoediae,: Juppiter certo prodit in tragoedia,: quae si prodierit, atque cum prodierit— scio enim proditurum esse—audiet,: si haec consuetudo prodire coeperit,: cum tot prodierint colores,have come up, become the fashion,: cultus et ornatus variis prodisse capillis Obfuit,: tu cum, projectis insignibus, prodis ex judice Dama Turpis, etc.,become manifest, turn out to be,: juvenum prodit Publica cura,.—
To go forwards, advance, proceed (class.): est quadam prodire tenus,: prodire sumptu extra modum,: prodeuntibus annis,with advancing years, in the course of time,.— Impers. pass.: ne ad extremum prodeatur,.

la:adj:prodigus.html:
prōdĭgus, a, um, adj.
prodigo
,
wasteful, lavish, prodigal.
Lit. (class.; syn.: largus, munificus): omnino duo sunt genera largorum, quorum alteri prodigi, alteri liberales. Prodigi, qui epulis et viscerationibus et gladiatorum muneribus, ludorum venationumque apparatu, pecunias profundunt in eas res, quarum memoriam aut levem aut nullam omnino sint relicturi,: femina,.—With gen.: peculii sui prodigus,: aeris,; .— As subst.: prōdĭgus, i, m., a wasteful person, a spendthrift, prodigal: largitor et prodigus,: lege XII. tabularum prodigo interdicitur bonorum suorum administratio, prooem.; ; : prodigus ad bonos mores reversus,, a, 12.—
Transf.
Causing great expense, costly, expensive (post-Aug.): margaritae, prodiga res,.—
Rich, abounding in any thing (poet.); with gen.: locus prodigus herbae,.—Absol.: tellus,rich, fertile,.—
Abundant, great, strong (post-Aug.): odor,: alvus,great, stout,.—
Trop., lavish, prodigal, profuse; with gen.: prodigus suae alienaeque et fortunae et pudicitiae,: arcanique Fides prodiga,: judicii sui,: animaeque magnae Prodigum Paulum,careless of life,; cf.: prodiga gens animae,.—With in and acc.: libidines in cibos atque in Venerem prodigae,: sed finem impensae non servat prodiga Roma,: prodiga corruptoris Improbitas,: prodigis oculis intueri, with greedy eyes, with voluptuous glances, Auct. .—Hence, adv.: prōdĭgē, lavishly, extravagantly, prodigally (class.): prodige vivere,: uti aliquā re,.

prōdĭgĭōsus, a, um, adj.
prodigium
,
unnatural, strange, wonderful, marvellous, prodigious (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): atria Circes,: cura Veneris,: mendacia,: corpora,; cf. : astra,: ostentatio (virium),: fides,: prodigiosum dictu!: ora prodigiosa Tartarei canis, mart. 5, 36, 2.—Comp.: quo nihil prodigiosius passa est respublica, Trebell. la:verb:prodigo.html:
prōdĭgo, ēgi, actum, 3, v. a.
pro-ago
,

Lit. (ante-class.): sues in lutosos limites,: in pabulum,med.: pulli prodigendi in solem,med. —
Transf., to get rid of.

In a bad sense, to squander, to lavish, waste, dissipate (not in Cic. or Cæs.; cf.: effundo, profundo, consumo): festo die si quid prodegeris,: suom,: aliena bona, Sall. Or. Lepidi contra Sull.: opes, Suet. ner. 30: sua,: illi prodigere vitam pro victoriā contendentes,: singulos artus suos fortunae prodigendos dare quaestu atque compendio gloriarum,.
